data.name: Army General
data.detailed_description:
Army General is a turnbased strategy game that depicts the desert warfare in Northern Afrika and parts of the Mediterranean sea during World War II.
Fight back the Italian invasion of Egypt in 1940 with the Desert Rats or advance to Suez with the Afrikakorps in 1941/42. Adjust your units to the challenges of each map by exchanging officers, equipment and subordinate units. Create your own maps and campaings for yourself or to share it with other players.

Main features

  • Detailed background maps as well as combat and movement animations
  • Highly customizable units that allow to form plenty of individual entities
  • More than 450 officers of ten nations, able to gain experience and evolve through battles
  • 250 different equipments for land, air and sea combat such as tanks, bombers and battleships
  • Different support units that are subordinate to the main unit and differ for nations and unit types
  • Editor to create your own scenarios and campaigns

Additional information

  • Divisions and regiments with different characteristics
  • 58 special parameters for unit types that influence game situations like attacks on special terrain
  • Keep your own army during a solo campaign
  • 20 scenarios that are combined in the German main campaign
  • 5 scenarios that form the British "Operation Compass" campaign
  • Tutorial series to introduce important aspects of the game

reviews.review:
After playing most of the Afrika Korps campaign I must say that I am positively impressed with this game. 

Short Story:
At first glance this game may look as just another Panzer General clone, in reality there are a number of well designed features in the game that offer a lot more options for stategic decision during the campaign. Potentially the game has a solid re-playability value. 

More in details:

Unit customisation. First you can buy battalion or brigate size units which have different cost and different combat statistics, then you can attach sub units (companies) to change some of the statistics of the parent unit and so customise your units to fit better for specific tasks. The units gain experience if they win battles. Of course more experienced units perform better; as a rule of thums a unit with 3 exp. levels has a performance ca. doubled compared to a green unit.  

Leaders. Each unit must have a leader attached to it. Each leader has different stats that can significantly alter the unit performance in many ways. Leaders are class specific and limited in number so your army composition is somehow determined / limited by their availability (e.g. you can not buy an artillery unit if there is not an artillery leader available).
The leader themselves evolve with the game. If they perform well they increase their statistics (thus making more powerful the units under their command), on the other hands, if a unit under a leader command takes a significant beating or is destroyed, the leader stats. may be reduced.
During the campaign, either by effect of player decisions or by taking on map objetives, you get more leaders. You can reassign the best leaders as you see fit, however this cost a lot of points (resouces), so between the campaign scenarios you really need to make deciosions such as: do I buy a new Tank or I replace that crappy leader of that high experience fighter? 


Combat mechanics. Many factors are considered in the determination of the combat outcome, and these are presented as a table before (as predictor) and after the combat (as detailed result) so you can look at which factor(s) contributed most to the loss ratio you had. That is a nice way to learn how to better use your equipment. 


OKW Favour points. In each mission you get a special task such as capturing a location, destroying enemy units,  saving your own units etc. When you get 3 points you can decide if you want to change them for more resources, get more leaders or just skip the decision later when you accumulate 6 or 9 points. Of course, with 6 and 9 points you can get far better rewards. I think this is very intersting because makes the campaing varying based on that you decide.   

Maps. Looks well drawn and clear, however, IMHO they do not blend well with the Nato counters and I prefer to see the tiny soldiers on the ground.

Area for improvement;
Note: the game is just released and most of the points below can be easily fixed. Consider also that most of this game is almost a one man effort, so it is quite impressive the quality level at launch. 

 
Unit sprites. I find the units too small and sometimes it is hard to see the differences between e.g. mountain inf. vs regular inf. or similar tank units. It looks that not much effort has been put on this aspect. 

Unit roster and Game interface. Same as above, the game offers a lot of options for the unit management/refit/upgrade but is a real pain look at all the small symbols at least for my old eyes :-)

Manual. There is one and contains useful info but there is no reference of its existence either in the product page or in the game menu. You have to find the PDF doc in the game root.

Overall the game needs some polishing (spelling) and have some naive things that ruin the immersion, however nothing that can not be fixed or modified in due course.
